text:
elena: Quick RFC follow-up — we need a short runbook for air-gapped probe failures and safe fallback behavior. Filed a bunch of edge cases in the doc but want everyone's take before I lock it down.

sam: +1. can you summarize the main open questions?

elena: Sure — three buckets: 1) probe semantics (how aggressive / how many retries), 2) what constitutes 'safe partial apply' vs full abort, 3) operator-visible signals and automated fallback rules.

maria: For probes: prefer fast fail on obvious mismatch (signature/version) and slower retries on network blips. Something like: immediate signature check -> if fails, abort. If signature OK but fetch fails, do exponential backoff with jitter up to N tries.

elena: Exactly. Proposed knobs in the draft: probe_timeout_ms=3000, max_probe_attempts=5, backoff_base_ms=500, jitter=20%. Also a 'probe-mode' enum: {fast-fail, conservative, manual-intervene}.

sam: That seems reasonable. For partial apply rules: we need a clear invariant — cluster must be left in a consistent state that operator can recover. So partial apply allowed only for non-root components and only if checksums for applied items verified.

trent: Small UX note: when partial apply happens we should emit a single aggregated event + 'last-successful-manifest' file an operator can curl from node. Otherwise triage is impossible.

elena: Good call. I'll add an artifact: /var/lib/redwood/last-successful-manifest.json and a human-readable summary in the node logs.

ops-bot: deploy started: airgap-probe job 4150001111 -> status: probe:attempt=1

maria: About signatures: verifier boundary needs to be strict. If the verifier can't validate a signature the node must never apply anything. No soft-fail. 

elena: Agreed. The verifier is an atomic gate. If it returns non-ok, we go to 'quarantine' mode with operator alert and no writes.

sam: What about fallback policies? Proposed policy levels: 
- level0: try local cache only, no external.
- level1: attempt fetch from masked mirror (operator-provided USB/registry).
- level2: operator-manual restore.

maria: Add an emergency 'rollback-to-last-success' auto-option but behind an opt-in flag. Useful for fleets that value availability > new features.

elena: Yes, flag name: auto_rollback_on_probe_failure (default false). If true, we will attempt atomic swap to last-successful-manifest. Must also block if signatures mismatch.

trent: Need clear telemetry: probe_attempts, probe_latency_ms, fallback_level_triggered, partial_apply_count, verifier_failures. Console should show per-node timeline.

ops-bot: probe result: attempt=2 status=timeout latency=3005ms

elena: On timeouts we should escalate: after 3 timeouts within probe_window (10m) bump to conservative mode and require operator acknowledgement to resume canary. Thoughts?

sam: Good safety. Also document operator steps: 1) check last-successful-manifest, 2) inspect node logs (grep redwood:quarantine), 3) if signatures OK, manually re-run fetch with `redwood-agent fetch --force-probe`, else initiate signing/registry fix. Keep steps short.

maria: Include a tiny snippet for the agent command in runbook: ```
# force a single fetch + verify
redwood-agent fetch --manifest /tmp/manifest.json --verify-only
redwood-agent apply --dry-run
```

elena: I'll add that. One more boundary callout: the agent must never auto-promote a partially-applied set into active state without a reconciliation pass that verifies all component checksums and the manifest graph. Put another way: apply -> staged -> reconcile -> activate. No shortcuts.

trent: And we should define a compact 'safety header' that travels with delta bundles: fields = [bundle_id, parent_manifest_id, min_required_checksum, signature_version]. That lets probe logic reject incompatible deltas early.

elena: Love it. I'll add JSON example in the RFC: ```
{"bundle_id":"b-2026-04-01","parent_manifest":"m-2026-03-30","min_checksum":"sha256:...","sig_v":"v2"}
```

sam: Last ops question: alerting thresholds — when do we page? I'd say page when verifier fails or when the node enters quarantine. Timeouts should be warnings first.

maria: Agreed. Pager for quarantine + repeated verifier failures. Slack alert for probe-level degradations.

elena: Thanks all — I'll update the doc with these concrete knobs, the small runbook steps, and the telemetry signals. If no objections I'll merge the follow-up by EOD and add the sample console mock. :shipit:

deploy-bot: thread closed: 4150001111 -> merged:airgap-probe-fallback-runbook v1
